# Submitting

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball. We review it, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset
and score it. That run determines its rank on the leaderboard. When the hackathon ends, your latest submission that
passed review runs once more, on a private dataset, in the [final run](#what-happens-next), which weighs most when we pick the winners.

## Package layout

```
agent.json          {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": ["qwen"]}
pyproject.toml      (or package.json, requirements.txt, ...)
agent.py            your code
```

- `agent.json` at the root: `setup` (optional) and `run`, each an argv array. Both run in the package directory.
  `browsers` (optional, 1 to 4, default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts for the run; see
  [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#browsers). `models` (optional) lists the hosted models your agent system calls,
  by provider id, all of them by default: the run's clock waits for those to warm up, and `[]` starts it right after
  setup; see [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#scored-run).
- At most 20 MB compressed; regular files only.
- No secrets: the run gets everything it needs from the environment.

## Upload

```
tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
  $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions
```

The response (`202`) has your submission's id. Review is still pending and no runs exist yet: follow it with
`GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` for the review result and run ids, or watch the leaderboard.

`$ATIRA_TOKEN` is your personal token: `atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser, and
`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).

Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.

## Test it in the sandbox first

Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
your team. Up to 4 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
test-run slot at once.

## Linking your GitHub repository

The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.

The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
settings.

## Watching your submission

Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
masked as `[private]`.

## Resubmitting

Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
can submit again.

## What happens next

1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),
   then your run command (timed).
3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and
   time; ineligible answers rank after every eligible one.
4. **Final run:** when the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review
   (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected and disqualified ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. It is the latest one, not the best one.
   That run weighs most when we pick the winners ([Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners)), so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to
   the public scenario. Its results stay with the organizers until they publish them; then the leaderboard shows
   the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", and the public-dataset board stays at
   `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

1	# Getting started: from sign-in to your first scored run
2	
3	How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.
4	
5	Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:
6	
7	```text
8	Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
9	```
10	
11	Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start) · The challenge: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)
12	
13	## What you're building
14	
15	Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
16	
17	## Your first test run
18	
19	Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.
20	
21	### 1. Sign in and form a team
22	
23	[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
24	
25	### 2. Install the CLI and sign in
26	
27	The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).
28	
29	macOS and Linux:
30	
31	```sh
32	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
33	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
34	atira login
35	```
36	
37	Windows, in PowerShell:
38	
39	```powershell
40	irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
41	atira login
42	```
43	
44	Optional: connect the coding agent you use (one line each):
45	
46	```sh
47	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
48	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
49	```
50	
51	### 3. Scout the websites yourself
52	
53	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)
54	
55	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
56	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
57	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
58	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
59	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
60	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
61	
62	### 4. Choose your starting point
63	
64	Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.
65	
66	macOS and Linux:
67	
68	```sh
69	mkdir my-agent
70	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
71	```
72	
73	Windows, in PowerShell:
74	
75	```powershell
76	mkdir my-agent
77	curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
78	tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
79	```
80	
81	### 5. Develop locally
82	
83	You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
84	
85	macOS and Linux:
86	
87	```sh
88	cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
89	eval "$(atira scout --env)"
90	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
91	```
92	
93	Windows, in PowerShell:
94	
95	```powershell
96	cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
97	atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
98	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
99	```
100	
101	Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
102	
103	### 6. Test in the sandbox
104	
105	The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
106	
107	```sh
108	atira test-run .
109	```
110	
111	### 7. Submit
112	
113	A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
114	
115	```sh
116	atira submit .
117	```
118	
119	## Unlimited Inference
120	
121	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
122	
123	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
124	
125	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
126	
127	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
128	- **Simulated pricing:**
129	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
130	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
131	  - Cache writes: Free
132	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
133	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
134	
135	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
136	
137	```python
138	import os
139	from openai import OpenAI
140	
141	qwen = OpenAI(
142	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
143	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
144	)
145	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
146	    model="qwen",
147	    messages=[{
148	        "role": "user",
149	        "content": "Which button submits?",
150	    }],
151	)
152	```
153	
154	### Cloudflare Clef
155	
156	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
157	
158	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
159	- **Simulated pricing:**
160	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
161	  - Output: Not priced
162	
163	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
164	
165	```sh
166	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
167	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
168	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
169	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
170	  "questions": {"next": {
171	    "type": "choice",
172	    "instructions": "What next?",
173	    "criteria": {
174	      "retry": "Retry the request",
175	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
176	```
177	
178	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
179	
180	```sh
181	atira login   # once per computer
182	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
183	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
184	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
185	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
186	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
187	```
188	
189	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
190	
191	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
192	
193	## Limits
194	
195	What every scored run gets.
196	
197	| Rule | What it means |
198	| --- | --- |
199	| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
200	| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
201	| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
202	| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
203	| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
204	| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
205	| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
206	| Team | Up to 5 people. |
207	
208	## How you're scored
209	
210	Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.
211	
212	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
213	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
214	
215	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
216	
217	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.
218	
219	On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.
220	
221	## Public and private data
222	
223	The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
224	
225	## Using a coding agent?
226	
227	Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.
228	
229	Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.
230	
231	```sh
232	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
233	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
234	```
235

| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |

### 4. Choose your starting point

Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.

macOS and Linux:

```sh
mkdir my-agent
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
mkdir my-agent
curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
```

### 5. Develop locally

You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).

macOS and Linux:

```sh
cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).

### 6. Test in the sandbox

The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.

```sh
atira test-run .
```

### 7. Submit

A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).

```sh
atira submit .
```

## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```sh
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
  "questions": {"next": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "What next?",
    "criteria": {
      "retry": "Retry the request",
      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```sh
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
| Team | Up to 5 people. |

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Using a coding agent?

Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.

Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
```

42	## Tools
43	
44	| Tool | What it does | About |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| `challenge_brief` | The challenge: task, websites, rules and limits, run contract, scoring and answer schema | 6k tokens |
47	| `list_runs` | Your team's recent test and scored runs: status, quality, cost, time and package | 50 tokens a run |
48	| `get_run` | One run: status and failure, queue place or warm-up while it waits, phases, package, model calls by model with failures and queue waits, points per field, recordings, answer, run page | 1–2k |
49	| `diagnose_run` | Why a run failed and whether to rerun it as it is: the failure class, the last 20 stdout and stderr lines, model errors, idle stretches over 60 s, browsers whose screen froze | 2–3k |
50	| `run_logs` | Log lines in time order, by time (`from`, `to`), stream, text (`grep`) and `browser`; `tail` for the last lines; page by page | 30 a line |
51	| `run_llm_calls` | Every model call, one line each, under a header with time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and, for models the organizers host, the queue wait | 35 a call |

54	| `run_inputs` | The clicks, scrolls and typing the platform recorded in each browser, with their times | 25 an input |
55	| `compare_runs` | Two runs side by side: package, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures per model, phases, points per field and answer fields that changed | 1–2k |
56	| `wait_for_run` | Wait until a run is running or done, including recording collection and scoring (at most `timeout_s`, default 50 s), then say how it stands | 300 |
57	| `list_submissions` | Your scored submissions: review status, any organizer note, result and package | 60 a submission |
58	| `get_submission` | One submission (`sub_...`): review status, any organizer note, its runs | 300–800 |
59	| `run_package` | The package a run or submission used, as uploaded: SHA-256, label, agent.json and each file's size, never the contents; `out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder | 15 a file |
60	| `leaderboard` | The board with each entry's cost × time and the Pareto front, your rank and the gap to the next; `compare_run` places one of your runs on it | 500 |
61	| `models` | The models the organizers host, if any, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` | 300 |
62	| `test_run` | Pack a folder and start a test run; returns its id, queue place, package SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) | 150 |
63	| `cancel_run` | Cancel one of your runs that hasn't finished; only with `confirm: true` | 60 |
64	| `submit` | Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run, public and final; only with `confirm: true` after the person said yes | 100 |
65	
66	Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
67	doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
68	you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".
69	
70	Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
71	`run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.

74	
75	`get_run` while a run waits, then once it failed:
76	
77	```
78	run_8af0981b3710558a · test run on the public dataset · package 3f2a1c9e0b12 (2 files) "a41c2d9-dirty"
79	Status queued, phase queued
80	Queued: 2 runs ahead of yours, starts in about 3 min
81	...
82	Status failed, phase done · Failure: Run exited with code 0 without submitting an answer (no answer)
83	```
84	
85	`run_llm_calls`:
86	
87	```
88	run_0d7f1203b576189a · 86 model calls in a run of 16:22 · $0.4130
89	Time in calls 6:41 · latency p50 2.1s, p95 31s · at most 4 at once (at 02:13)
90	  anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5: 33 calls, $0.4126, 57,619 in (72,128 cached) / 5,867 out, 2:05 in calls
91	  openai/gpt-5-mini: 1 call, $0.0004, 1,845 in / 12 out, 1.2s in calls
92	Failures: openai: 52 failed (429 rate limited)
93	
94	[02:10.4 +3.2s] anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200 in 4,210 (cached 3,900) out 312 $0.00471 id=c_812
95	[02:13.9 +0.4s] openai 429 rate limited $0.00 id=c_815
96	```
97	
98	`run_profile` (the screen columns are seconds the browser's screen was changing; `–` is still):
99	
100	```
101	time   b1 in · screen  b2 in · screen  b3 in · screen  b4 in · screen  calls  in calls  busy  cost
102	02:00  6 · 21s         3 · 8.0s        10 · 44s        0 · –           14     1:02      48s   $0.0612
103	03:00  4 · 12s         0 · –           0 · –           2 · 3.5s        3      41s       38s   $0.0140
104	Critical path:
105	Longest stretches over 10 s with no input, no screen change and no model call in flight:
106	  03:12.4–04:40.1 (01:27)
107	    last line before: [03:11.9] stdout: mail TAN: waiting for the TAN message
108	Browsers that went quiet:
109	  browser 3: last screen change at 02:45.4, then nothing for 04:53 until the end
110	```
111	
112	`diagnose_run` names the failure's class and the next step: `cancelled`, `no answer` (your agent system ended
113	without entering one: fix it, a rerun alone won't help), `agent exit` (see stderr), `timeout` (make it faster),
114	`answer rejected` (fix the answer's shape) or `platform` (not your agent system: rerun it as it is). A reason that
115	starts with "Setup" is agent.json's setup: `run_logs` with stream `setup` shows why. Where the platform records a
116	run's failure class, that one is used.
117	
118	## Times
119	
120	Times are on the run's clock, as the run page shows them: `02:13`, `1:02:13`, `3m20s` or `133` seconds from the
121	run's start, or an ISO 8601 time; durations are written the same way. The same time in the run page's address,
122	`?t=02:13`, opens the replay there. Links point at the platform's own address, whichever name the CLI talks to.
123	
124	A screenshot is cut from the recording with ffmpeg on the platform. If the platform can't do that right now, the
125	CLI cuts it with your own ffmpeg (`brew install ffmpeg`, or `sudo apt install ffmpeg`); without one it says so and
126	links the replay. A time outside a recording gets its nearest frame and says so ("browser 1's recording covers
127	-00:03.7–07:48.9").

130	
131	- **Past frames of a live run.** The recording is stored after the run ends and collection finishes; until then `run_screenshot` shows each
132	  browser's latest live frame, about a second behind the screen (its time says when), and
133	  filmstrips and screen activity wait for the end. The run page's live view shows it moving.
134	- **Logs as they arrive.** Tools answer once; `wait_for_run` waits up to 600 s if your client allows long tool calls
135	  (Codex stops a tool after 60 s unless you raise `tool_timeout_sec`). In a terminal, `atira logs <run> --follow`
136	  streams a run's logs until it ends.
137	- **Log streams** are `setup`, `stdout`, `stderr` and `input`: errors are in `stderr` and in `get_run`/`diagnose_run`,
138	  screen activity is in `run_profile`.
139	- **Typed secrets.** Inputs show typed text with keys, tokens and your run's secrets masked.
140	
141	From a terminal, `atira cancel <run>` cancels a run and `atira status` lists your submissions and test runs.
142	
143	## Try it
144	
145	Ask your agent things like:
146	
147	- "Why did my last test run fail? Diagnose it, then show me the screen at the moment it went idle."
148	- "Where did the time go in run_19932ad4ade523e4? Which model calls were slowest?"
149	- "Compare my last two test runs: what changed in the score and the cost?"
150	- "Start a test run of ./my-agent, wait until it's running, and show me every browser's screen at 01:00."
151	- "Which files did my latest submission's package have? Save it to ./downloaded and diff it against ./my-agent."
152	
153	This guide is at `$API/docs/mcp.md`.

Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".

Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
`run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.

## What it shows

```

Status queued, phase queued
Queued: 2 runs ahead of yours, starts in about 3 min
...
Status failed, phase done · Failure: Run exited with code 0 without submitting an answer (no answer)
```

```

Time in calls 6:41 · latency p50 2.1s, p95 31s · at most 4 at once (at 02:13)
  anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5: 33 calls, $0.4126, 57,619 in (72,128 cached) / 5,867 out, 2:05 in calls
  openai/gpt-5-mini: 1 call, $0.0004, 1,845 in / 12 out, 1.2s in calls
Failures: openai: 52 failed (429 rate limited)

[02:10.4 +3.2s] anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200 in 4,210 (cached 3,900) out 312 $0.00471 id=c_812
[02:13.9 +0.4s] openai 429 rate limited $0.00 id=c_815
```

`run_profile` (the screen columns are seconds the browser's screen was changing; `–` is still):

```
time   b1 in · screen  b2 in · screen  b3 in · screen  b4 in · screen  calls  in calls  busy  cost
02:00  6 · 21s         3 · 8.0s        10 · 44s        0 · –           14     1:02      48s   $0.0612
03:00  4 · 12s         0 · –           0 · –           2 · 3.5s        3      41s       38s   $0.0140
Critical path:
Longest stretches over 10 s with no input, no screen change and no model call in flight:
  03:12.4–04:40.1 (01:27)
    last line before: [03:11.9] stdout: mail TAN: waiting for the TAN message
Browsers that went quiet:
  browser 3: last screen change at 02:45.4, then nothing for 04:53 until the end
```

`diagnose_run` names the failure's class and the next step: `cancelled`, `no answer` (your agent system ended
without entering one: fix it, a rerun alone won't help), `agent exit` (see stderr), `timeout` (make it faster),
`answer rejected` (fix the answer's shape) or `platform` (not your agent system: rerun it as it is). A reason that
starts with "Setup" is agent.json's setup: `run_logs` with stream `setup` shows why. Where the platform records a
run's failure class, that one is used.

## Times

Times are on the run's clock, as the run page shows them: `02:13`, `1:02:13`, `3m20s` or `133` seconds from the
run's start, or an ISO 8601 time; durations are written the same way. The same time in the run page's address,
`?t=02:13`, opens the replay there. Links point at the platform's own address, whichever name the CLI talks to.

A screenshot is cut from the recording with ffmpeg on the platform. If the platform can't do that right now, the
CLI cuts it with your own ffmpeg (`brew install ffmpeg`, or `sudo apt install ffmpeg`); without one it says so and
links the replay. A time outside a recording gets its nearest frame and says so ("browser 1's recording covers
-00:03.7–07:48.9").

## What it can't do

- **Past frames of a live run.** The recording is stored after the run ends and collection finishes; until then `run_screenshot` shows each
  browser's latest live frame, about a second behind the screen (its time says when), and
  filmstrips and screen activity wait for the end. The run page's live view shows it moving.
- **Logs as they arrive.** Tools answer once; `wait_for_run` waits up to 600 s if your client allows long tool calls
  (Codex stops a tool after 60 s unless you raise `tool_timeout_sec`). In a terminal, `atira logs <run> --follow`
  streams a run's logs until it ends.
- **Log streams** are `setup`, `stdout`, `stderr` and `input`: errors are in `stderr` and in `get_run`/`diagnose_run`,
  screen activity is in `run_profile`.
- **Typed secrets.** Inputs show typed text with keys, tokens and your run's secrets masked.

From a terminal, `atira cancel <run>` cancels a run and `atira status` lists your submissions and test runs.

## Try it

Ask your agent things like:

- "Why did my last test run fail? Diagnose it, then show me the screen at the moment it went idle."
- "Where did the time go in run_19932ad4ade523e4? Which model calls were slowest?"
- "Compare my last two test runs: what changed in the score and the cost?"
- "Start a test run of ./my-agent, wait until it's running, and show me every browser's screen at 01:00."
- "Which files did my latest submission's package have? Save it to ./downloaded and diff it against ./my-agent."

This guide is at `$API/docs/mcp.md`.

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

A run's `phase` moves through `queued`, `provisioning`, `setup`, `running`, `scoring` and `done`; its `status`
ends as `scored` or `submitted` (an answer was scored), `failed` or `timed_out`. Each run carries `dataset`:
`"public"` for test runs and scored runs during the hackathon, `"private"` for the final run. On a private dataset,
`scenario_id` is left out and `error` and `answer` are `null`: they stay with the organizers.

A failed run says why in `failure_class`: `platform` (the platform failed, not your agent system: a sandbox fault, a
lost connection, our own timeout, or a hosted model down for most of the run), `agent_exit` (setup or the run exited
non-zero), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `no_answer` (it exited 0 without an answer) or `answer_rejected` (every answer it
sent was invalid); `null` while it runs and once it succeeded. A `platform` failure has `counts: false`: it counts
toward neither the ranking nor any limit, and its `error` reads "The platform failed, not your agent system. This
run doesn't count; start it again." A scored run is queued again once by itself, as the run named in `retry_run_id`
(whose `retry_of` names this one), and its `error` ends "it was started again automatically." instead.

### Cancelling a run

```sh
curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/cancel" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Your team cancels its own test runs and scored runs that have not finished (organizers can cancel any run). The run
stops at once: its execution is aborted, its sandbox removed, its recording stopped and its live links revoked. It
ends as `failed` with the error `Cancelled by @you` and `finished_at` set, and your team can start the next test run
straight away. A queued run is cancelled before it starts. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not
complete: the leaderboard ignores that submission and you can submit again. `200` returns `{"run_id", "status": "failed", "error",
"finished_at"}`; `404` means no such run of yours, `409` that it has already finished. In a browser session, send
the `x-atira-csrf` header as for every write.

### Logs

Test runs and scored runs keep their output. Read it from a cursor: each page holds up to 128 chunks and the cursor
to continue from.

```sh
cursor=0
while :; do
  page=$(curl -s "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN")
  printf '%s' "$page" | jq -j '.chunks[].text'
  next=$(printf '%s' "$page" | jq .cursor)
  [ "$next" = "$cursor" ] && break
  cursor=$next
done
```

While the run is live, keep polling with a pause until `feed` reports `phase` `done` and its `log_cursor` is no
newer than yours. Or follow them as they arrive, as server-sent events:

```sh
curl -N "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/stream?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Each event is one chunk: `id` is its cursor and `data` is `{"at", "stream", "text"}`. Reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` (an `EventSource` does this by itself) or `?after=` to resume. A comment line (`: heartbeat`) comes
every 15 seconds; once the run has finished and everything is sent, an `end` event closes the stream, and connecting
again answers `204`. All of it at once, as JSON lines:

```sh
curl -o logs.jsonl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs.jsonl" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

To look at one stretch of a run, query its lines by time and content. Times are on the run's clock, as the run page
shows them: `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `3m20s` or seconds from the run's start (a minus is before it), or an ISO 8601 time.

```sh
curl -G "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/query" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode from=02:10 --data-urlencode to=02:40 --data-urlencode stream=stdout,stderr \
  --data-urlencode 'grep=error|timeout'
```

It answers `lines` (each with `t`, its milliseconds from the start, `clock` as `mm:ss.s`, `at`, `stream` and `text`),
`matched` and `next`: up to `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 1,000), and `next` to pass as `after` while more
match. `grep` is case-insensitive text; `a|b` matches either. The `input` stream holds the clicks, scrolls and typing
the platform recorded in each browser, one line per action (`browser 1: click at 640,412`). Typed text is shown, with
keys, tokens, your run's secrets and password or one-time-code fields masked. Lines come in time order across
streams. A click, drag or drop gives its point on the browser's 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included) and, when
the platform knew the page's geometry, the same point in the page's viewport with the viewport's size:
`browser 1: click at 200,685 (viewport 200,542 of 1279x656)`. Frames and recordings show the viewport alone, so that
point lands on a frame at 200/1279 of its width and 542/656 of its height.

`GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/llm-calls` lists the run's model calls in order (`at`, `provider`, `model`, `status`, tokens,
`cost_micro_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `queue_ms`, how long a call to a hosted model waited for a GPU), up to `limit`
(2,000 by default) with `next` to pass as `after`. `GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/screen-activity` gives, per browser, the
spans during which its screen kept changing: a gap between spans is a time the screen sat still.

Runs on the public dataset (test runs and scored runs during the hackathon) keep their logs unredacted. On a
private dataset (the final run), your logs and the feed's `error` have private values masked as `[private]`.

16:- **Cost:** the run's LLM usage, priced per model, in USD.

31:3. Lower cost × time: the submission's cost in USD times its time, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time
32:   as at least 1 second. Cost and time weigh the same: halving your model bill counts as much as halving your run

40:never the expected values. Runs on the private dataset show quality, eligibility, cost and time without a breakdown.
## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission on the private set. The default is one attempt.
Before the final run starts, opt in to **Best of 3** on your team page or run
`atira final --best-of 3` (`--best-of 1` opts out). `atira status` shows the choice.
When the final run starts, each team's choice is fixed, including teams still in review.
Opted-in teams get up to three attempts on the same private scenario(s). Your **single best complete attempt**
counts: eligible first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time, with the leaderboard's usual floors.
It is not an average, and a failed attempt does not outweigh a better successful one.
Every attempt is kept. Your team sees its own attempts' logs (private values masked) and, once the organizers publish the final, the results.
Calls using your own model keys can cost up to **3×**. The public leaderboard remains one run per submission
on the public scenario. Review, flags and disqualification work as for any submission.

content.text:
Most of my slice checks out against the docs. I found no outright factual errors, just one unverifiable claim and several gaps.

**Confirmed correct:** test-run 2 h vs scored 20 min; setup up to 5 min with network, not timed; time runs from the start of the `run` command to the accepted answer; 400 keeps the clock running; `seconds_left` plus "submit about a minute early"; `browsers` 1 to 4; 20 MB package; one submission in flight (429). Also correct: the Qwen and Clef prices and the 32 and 16 concurrency limits, `QWEN_*` / `CLEF_*`, `--best-of 3` costing up to 3x on own keys, the local dev commands, and the MCP add line.

## 1. Wrong or unverifiable
- **Concurrency "(raised by organizers, may change)":** I can't verify the "raised" part. docs_api.md "The run queue" says up to 4 test runs run at once, up to 3 more can wait, and one more gets 429.
- **Score breakdown "same" for both kinds of run:** true on the public dataset. The final private run shows quality, eligibility, cost and time with no breakdown, and its logs have private values replaced by `[private]` (docs_scoring.md, docs_api.md).
- **`models` in `agent.json`:** the doc doesn't say what happens when the field is missing. Without it the run waits for every hosted model. The starter kit sets `["qwen"]`, so if you start using Clef, add `"clef"`. Otherwise Clef may still be warming up when your timed run starts (run-contract "Scored run").
- **Package limits:** besides 20 MB, the limits are 2,000 files and 5 MB per file. `.gitignore` exclusions apply (docs_cli.md).

## 2. Missing practical info
- **Setup vs run:** setup gets no run variables and no team secrets, and nothing it starts carries over into the run. Model warm-up (up to 10 min) is also not timed.
- **Team secrets:** max 20; names in capitals, digits and underscores; reserved names are refused (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `CDP_URL(S)`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, ...). They can also be managed with `PUT/GET/DELETE /v1/teams/me/secrets/<NAME>`. Values are redacted from logs. Source: run-contract "Team secrets".
- **Sandbox environment:** `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` (JSON array), `BROWSER_COUNT`, and `DISPLAY` (`:n`). `HTTP(S)_PROXY=127.0.0.1:3128` is the only way out, with `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1`. Any custom HTTP client must respect these. Locally `CDP_URLS` is not set and the kit launches its own Chromium (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). `browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches to browser 2, since the index starts at 0.
- **User-Agent:** send your own. The API answers Python's default `Python-urllib` with 403.
- **After a 202:** the agent has 10 s to exit before the platform stops it.
- **CLI commands to add:**
  - `atira cancel <run_|reh_>` (409 / exit 6 if the run already finished)
  - `atira logs <run> --follow`
  - `atira status [id]`, which also shows the best-of choice
  - `atira package <id> --out`
  - `atira final` with no flag shows the current choice; `--best-of 1` opts out
  - `test-run --dry-run` shows what would be uploaded
  - `atira upgrade` fixes "Unknown command: models"
- **Exit codes:** 3 not signed in, 5 bad package, 6 busy/429, 7 `--follow` run failed or timed out. Worth noting for scripts.
- **MCP tools that pay off when debugging:** `diagnose_run` (failure class plus last stderr), `run_logs` (grep and time range), `run_llm_calls` (cost, p50/p95 latency, queue wait), `run_profile` (critical path, idle stretches), `run_screenshot`, `compare_runs`, `cancel_run`. Failure classes: `platform`, `agent_exit`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `no_answer`, `answer_rejected`.
- **Platform failures:** if the hosted models were down for most of a run that ended with no answer, the run doesn't count, and a scored run restarts once by itself.
- **Measuring cost:** `/v1/runs/current` shows spend so far, `GET /v1/models/status` lists hosted-model prices, and `run_llm_calls` gives per-model totals. Cached input and thinking tokens are billed; a call with no reported cost is charged the highest published price; there is no spending limit.
- **Install:** after installing, run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` (start.md).
- **Local proxy:** `atira models proxy` listens on port 8765. Use `--port` together with `atira scout --env --port`.

## 3. Cut
- The "(raised by organizers, may change)" aside.
- Models bullet 3 ("Locally: ..."): it repeats the dev-loop block word for word.
- The "Cold start can take minutes" warning applies only locally, since warm-up isn't timed in runs. Shorten it to "locally, use long timeouts (kit: 360 s)".
- Outside my slice, but "Why the leaderboard has few entries" is a dated snapshot (2026-10-10) and will go stale.
